title: Fixed-endpoint shuffles give longer frequency paths than observed in 33 selected CHIME events
abstract: We test fitted component order in CHIME/FRB Catalog 2 release 20251231. We hold the first and last peak frequencies fixed and permute only the internal peaks. In 33 events from 20 source labels, equal source weights give a normalized observed path length of 1.306 and a conditional shuffle mean of 1.604. The observed path is 18.6 percent shorter. The mean difference is 0.298, with a 95 percent source bootstrap interval of 0.124 to 0.486. None of 100000 conditional shuffle trials has an equal or shorter path. The result remains after removal of FRB20220912A. For events with exactly four components, the reduction is 8.0 percent and the bootstrap interval includes zero. The test finds order beyond the known endpoint direction under exchangeable internal peak positions. It does not measure continuous drift, establish an emission model, or confirm a new source. Missing peak errors, shared fits, component selection and instrument response limit physical claims. No independent telescope data confirm this test. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: The observed frequency path and conditional shuffled paths. The source bootstrap intervals describe variation across source labels. They do not include fit errors.
